### Calculation of Hardness

First, convert all salt equivalents to equivalent amounts of calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$):
$$\text{Equivalent of } CaCO_3 = \text{Given mass of salt (mg/L)} \times \frac{\text{Molar mass of } CaCO_3 (100)}{\text{Molar mass of salt}}$$

1. **$Ca(HCO_3)_2$** = $170 \times \frac{100}{162} = 104.94\text{ mg/L}$ (Temporary)
2. **$Mg(HCO_3)_2$** = $85 \times \frac{100}{146} = 58.22\text{ mg/L}$ (Temporary)
3. **$MgCl_2$** = $90 \times \frac{100}{95} = 94.74\text{ mg/L}$ (Permanent)
4. **$CaSO_4$** = $146 \times \frac{136}{136}$ (Wait, molar mass of $CaSO_4 = 40 + 32 + 64 = 136$): $146 \times \frac{100}{136} = 107.35\text{ mg/L}$ (Permanent)

* **Temporary Hardness:** Sum of carbonates and bicarbonates
  $$\text{Temporary Hardness} = 104.94 + 58.22 = 163.16\text{ mg/L (or ppm)}$$
* **Permanent Hardness:** Sum of chlorides and sulfates
  $$\text{Permanent Hardness} = 94.74 + 107.35 = 202.09\text{ mg/L (or ppm)}$$
* **Total Hardness:** $\text{Temporary} + \text{Permanent} = 163.16 + 202.09 = 365.25\text{ mg/L (or ppm)}$
proTip: Always multiply by $(100 / \text{Molar mass of salt})$ to convert any hardness-causing salt into equivalent $CaCO_3$.
